recipes.name: Gluten Free Banana Bread
ingredients_raw: 2 cups gluten-free all purpose baking flour

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x5 inch loaf pan.

In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder and salt. In a separate bowl, cream together butter and sugar. Stir in eggs, maple syrup and mashed bananas until well blended. Add the banana mixture to the flour mixture; mix until batter is just moist. Pour batter into prepared loaf pan.

Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 30 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into center of the loaf comes out clean. If using muffin or cupcake tins, bake for 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Gluten Free Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: A yummy, kid-approved gluten-free banana bread that will satisfy your pickiest eaters!

review.reviewBody: Good ! You can replace the sugar with a bit of honey and also add vanilla extract.Texture is good and you can play around with different types of G/F flour mixtures and still get a tasty result...
Very easy to make. Because I didn't have overripe bananas, I microwaved some half-ripe bananas on 30% power, checking every 20 seconds. With brown rice flour, needed to bake for 32 minutes.

I have made several gluten-free breads/cakes since going gluten-free January 2013. It takes some research and practice to get the right combination of flours. I used the gf flour recipe that already has xanthan gum in it but not all gf flour mixtures do. Read the label if you buy a pre-made mix. Xanthan gum or guar gum are absolutely necessary in this recipe. When adding the flour to the wet mixture, mix for at least a few minutes with an electric mixer, not just until mixed like the recipe says. That gets the flours/gum to work together better. I used 1/2 cup granulated sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar in place of the turbinado and syrup. Creamed those for several minutes with margarine and 2 tsp vanilla then added eggs and 6 medium very ripe bananas. My muffins were done in 20 minutes and raised pretty well. I got 18 out of this recipe. I am very happy with how they turned out.

I made it with cafe gluten free flour and 5 bananas and used coconut sugar added nutmeg and cinnamon , I baked it in a glass loaf pan greased with coconut oil and cafe gluten free flour then I mixed 1/4 cup of coconut sugar and tablespoon of maple syrup and some cinnamon and took a knife and swirled it on top before baking some pecan would have been a great addition , I baked for 30 min at 350 but was still not done lowered to 300 and baked till done checking every 12 min with a took pick it was moist and so very good like a cake saving this recipe forever Enjoy!

WONDERFUL base recipe for banana muffins - FINALLY I CAN BAKE AGAIN! Mine were not vegan (I used the 2 eggs) but I did use 1/2 cup of vegan stick butter. I used 2 cups of white rice flour, 3 tablespoons of apple sauce instead of maple syrup because I had none in my pantry. I only had 4 bananas so I went with that. I also added 2 teaspoons of cinnamon and 4 teaspoons of ground flaxseed meal. My 2 teenage boys (who don't eat dairy free/GF like mom has to do) RAVED about them. I used a Pampered Chef muffin stone tray to cook them in and this recipe filled it completely; between letting the oveN heat with the stone tray + baking time it was roughly 38 mins in my oven. These are moist and even better, don't cost $3.00 a piece like they do in the health food store. Thank you for this recipe!

I followed this recipe exactly except that substituted turbinado sugar with raw cane sugar - it's all I had in hand. I mixed all the wet together in the stand mixer for quite some time (10 minutes or more) to thaw the bananas a bit more. I mixed the dry ingredients separately - Robin Hood Nutri Gluten Free flour blend, baking powder and a bit of xanthan gum (1tsp)... and then I blended tighten together. I used 6 bananas and so the batter was enough to completely fill one loaf pan - it took 55-60 minutes to cook through.

I've made this recipe a dozen times. I have to say, it's quite a pain and I have to diverge from the recipe instructions to make it work, but I really enjoy the taste. I'm not culinarily advanced enough to know how to fix the issues I keep running into with it, but I'll just report what I've learned.

I cannot make this recipe in a loaf pan. It does not cook all the way through. I once left it in the oven for an hour and the middle was still completely uncooked batter while the outside was burnt. This has happened to me several times.

The best (and for me, only) way to make this recipe is with a muffin or cupcake tin, and liners. I will fill the cups 2/3 of the way and cook for about 20-25 minutes. Once they're done baking, I take them out and chill them in the fridge. 

Once they've completely cooled, I can peel the paper off. If I desire, I can then rewarm them in the toaster oven. But if I try to peel the paper off while they're still hot, half of it sticks to the paper. But chilled, they come off super clean. 

The other thing that helps immensely is adding a scoop or two of vanilla protein powder. Makes them more protein packed, and helps thicken the batter so it cooks easier!

I don't know if I'm just making this recipe wrong or what, but this is the only way I can get it to work. But once it's made, it's glorious. Great for when I have a little bit of hunger that I want to stave off for a larger meal, or a quick pre-breakfast in the morning.

Really impressed with my first GF baking. I made my own flour blend after consulting with a specialty whole food retailer (1/2C cornmeal flour, 1/2C white rice flour, 1/2C coconut flour, 1/4C almond meal, 1/4C rice bran)...used a 50/50 Splenda/coconut sugar blend, olive oil spread instead of butter and added 1ts vanilla, 1ts cinnamon and 1/2C chopped macadamia nuts. Sprinkled a little coconut sugar on the top. I baked this in a mini loaf pan (8 loaves) for about 45 minutes. So yummy, love the texture of the different flours. Want to add some chopped dates next time. I plan on having this as my easy breakfast, so full of goodness.

I used 1 1/4c bobs red mill gluten free flour mix, 3/4c almond/hazelnut flour, I added 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp vanilla, 1tsp cinn, and a dash or two of nutmeg. This made 6 generously sized "mega muffins". I did not use maple syrup, as my bananas were VERY ripe and very sweet. I resisted the temptation to add nuts or choc chips, but I may next time. these rose very well, I cooked for just under 30 min. The tops are a little crusty around the edges, the inside is moist and dense just like banana bread should be. I think next time I will try a different ratio of spices, as it just needs a little "zing", but overall, I am very pleased with the result!

Good. I like that there are fewer ingredients. I too changed it up a bit after reading the comments. 3 ripe normal size organic bananas, 2 tsp. Baking powder, added vanilla, hammered out pecans, 1/2 cup sugar free chocolate chips, left out the maple syrup, used Stevia. Baked at 350 for 30minutes
I added 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp vanilla extract, and 1/2 cup chopped walnuts. I'd recommend testing with a toothpick and it may need extra time to be all the way cooked.

The recipe did not bake in 20-30 min at 350. I baked for 55 min And it came out good. I also added xanthan gum, per another review. And some chocolate chips cause I love bananas bread with chocolate chips. Ooooh. Also, other reviews said to use less bananas, so I used 3. So. I would make this again.

Good base recipe. Followed all instructions for amounts / ingredients (used cup4cup flour) but added to those as follows: Added 1 cup pecans (crushed) &1 t vanilla Cooked in 12 muffin cups @350 for 18 mins. These were delicious.
Too many bananas. Had to cook longer than said. Was still soggy
DId not turn out...too liquidy after the alloted time.
Good flavor. Not alot of sugar. No way will it bake in 30 minutes. Try 60-70 min

LOVE this recipe! I used King Arthur's All-Purpose GF flour, Wholesome Yum Allulose instead of Turbinado, and 4 bananas instead of 6. I did bake an extra 5 minutes (probably could have gone another 5-10). Came out delicious! Definitely on the heavy/dense side, but so yummy and (somewhat) guilt-free.

I used almond flour, which was fine, but others were right, this calls for waay too many bananas. Waste of expensive flour. Even cooked for an hour and it was dark but still giggly. I may try to let it cool and then cut it and try to re-bake it
Didn't have maple syrup. Used honey instead.
